producer_report.summary: Root cause: each place that piped input to a child wrote all of stdin before reading stdout. Once the child's output passed the 64 KB pipe buffer, both sides blocked. I added `athena_git::output_with_stdin(&mut Command, Option<&[u8]>) -> io::Result<Output>`. It writes stdin on a scoped thread while the main thread collects stdout and stderr. A BrokenPipe on the write is ignored, because the child's exit status is the real signal. Any other write error is returned after the child has been waited for. `Git::exit` and the gitleaks runner (`secrets.rs`) now call it. The xtask `policy.rs` `git()` helper gets the same thread-and-drain fix locally. xtask can't depend on athena-git because of the dependency-graph policy test, so I left `xtask/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `docs/architecture.md` unchanged. Two new athena-git tests cover the fix. One pipes 3 MB through `cat`. The other writes 3 MB to a child that exits without reading and checks there is no error or hang. A "Fixed" entry is added to CHANGELOG.md.

checks_run.note: I ran the formatter, not `--check`. It reformatted in place and printed nothing.
The first run failed on `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations`. I fixed it and the re-run was clean.
Every suite passed, including the xtask policy tests, which completed instead of hanging. I did not read the full verbose output of the earlier `cargo test --locked` run, only this quiet re-run.

open_issues: The brief lists `xtask/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `docs/architecture.md` as deliverables, but I changed none of them. Using the shared helper from xtask would need an xtask to athena-git edge. That would break the policy test and need an architecture doc change. If the owner wants that edge, it is a separate decision.
I did not run `cargo fmt --all --check` as a separate command. I ran `cargo fmt --all`, which formats in place.
mistakes: My first helper used `unwrap_or_else(|_| Ok(()))`, which clippy rejected. I changed it to `unwrap_or(Ok(()))`.
I tried to read the saved verbose test output outside the working directory. The policy hook denied it, so I re-ran the tests with `-q` instead.
learnings: `xtask` has no dependency on `athena-git`, and the policy test pins the dependency graph, so it needs its own local helper.
`GateError` converts from `io::Error`, so the runner needed no new error variant.
